evidence:
segments: Vec::new(),
// per glyph: pen built in rasterize_indexed, then pushed to by every outline segment
fix: Keep a reusable scratch segment buffer in RasterFont (e.g. add `scratch: Mutex<Vec<Segment>>` next to `hinters`). In rasterize_indexed, take it with `std::mem::take` under the lock, call `clear()`, build the SegmentPen with `segments: scratch`, and store `pen.segments` back when done (on every return path). Alternatively pass `&mut Vec<Segment>` into `outline`. This removes the per-glyph Vec allocation and its growth reallocations on atlas misses.

// drops bitmaps, glyphs and runs capacity on every flush, which the design comment at 168 retains on purpose
fix: If steady-state reuse is preferred over releasing idle memory, replace the reset with `self.bitmaps.clear(); self.glyphs.clear(); self.runs.clear(); self.staged_bytes = 0;` (keeping capacity, optionally trimming above a threshold). This is a deliberate trade-off documented at lines 168-169, so only change it if the idle-retention cost is judged acceptable; otherwise leave as is.
